title: The emitted store builds a verified TLS configuration
when: Builds a database configuration with sslmode verify-full.
then: Expects a TLS configuration that verifies the server and requires TLS 1.2 or later.

title: The emitted store refuses each weak sslmode
when: Builds a database configuration for each weak sslmode while the test exception setting is 0.
then: Expects each weak mode refused.

title: The emitted store keeps the loopback exception narrow
when: Builds a database configuration for each host while the test exception setting is 1, and then for each other value of the setting.
then: Expects plaintext allowed only to a literal loopback address, an unverified TLS fallback refused, and a safe error for any other value of the setting.

title: The emitted store checks the chain, the server name and the TLS version on a real connection
when: Opens a real TLS connection with a valid certificate, then with a wrong server name, then with a wrong trust root.
then: Expects the valid certificate accepted and both failures refused.

title: The cursor value is bound and related access holds
when: Reads under a related access filter, then with an injection string as the cursor, then after deleting one related row with CursorAll.
then: Expects only the two permitted rows, no hidden row for the injection cursor, and the deleted related row granting no access.
notes: Proved by TestCursorBindsInputAndKeepsRelatedAccess; its name or a subtest must carry this ID. Partial: the cursor test shows the access filter is kept on list reads; no test yet covers single reads and writes.

title: A target value is a bound parameter
when: Creates and deletes a Placement whose target holds quotes, a placeholder, a non-ASCII character, a backslash and brackets, observes with an empty, oversized, invalid UTF-8 and NUL target, then with the real one.
then: Expects the four invalid targets refused and the opaque target completing its owner.
notes: Proved by TestOpaqueTargetValuesStayBoundParameters; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: An invalid key page request runs no query
when: On an uninitialized store, requests pages with a wrong-case entity, an empty and an oversized scope, a cursor with NUL, invalid UTF-8 and 257 bytes, limits of 0, 1001 and -1, a nil context, and a canceled context.
then: Expects ErrResourceState for every invalid request and the nil context, and Canceled for the canceled one, with no query possible.
notes: Proved by TestResourceStateKeysRejectInvalidInput; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The revision counts every write and ignores the caller
when: Creates a record with a caller revision of 800, updates through raw SQL with a forged revision, writes with the old observation, writes with the current revision and a forged value, replaces ordinarily, and migrates again.
then: Expects revision 1 at insert, 2 after raw SQL, ErrVersionConflict with no change for the old observation, 3 after the accepted conditional write, 4 after the replace, and 4 after the repeated migration.
notes: Proved by TestResourceVersionCoversAllWritesAndRejectsOldObservation; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: Only one concurrent conditional writer succeeds
when: Runs two conditional writes against revision 1 at the same time.
then: Expects exactly one success, one ErrVersionConflict, and revision 2.
notes: Proved by TestOnlyOneConcurrentVersionWriterSucceeds; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A conflict rolls back the transaction's other work
when: Creates another record and then writes conditionally with a stale revision in one transaction.
then: Expects ErrVersionConflict, the other record absent, and the target revision unchanged.
notes: Proved by TestResourceVersionConflictRollsBackWork; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A cursor page follows the database order with one query
when: Under the C and the ICU collation, creates six mixed-case records with two deleted, then pages through CursorLive, CursorAll and CursorDeleted with a limit of 2, selected fields, an implicit filter and a text match, counting queries, and finally lists ordinarily.
then: Expects one SELECT and no count per page, at most two rows, the database's own order even where it differs from Go string order, exact More and NextID, the right visibility per mode, and the ordinary list keeping its count.
notes: Proved by TestCursorPagesUseDatabaseOrderWithoutCounts; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: Every list predicate uses the current observation
when: With standard_conforming_strings off and a declared unobserved value holding a backslash, quote and placeholder, makes one stale and one current observation, then runs a scope, an implicit filter, a row filter, a text match, two related filters and a confirmed filter through List, ReadCursor and CountOnly, reads sparse lists, orders by the field, and deletes the stale row.
then: Expects the stored value kept in Get, every predicate and count matching the projected value, the cursor agreeing, sparse rows keeping their metadata, the order using the projection, and the deleted row absent.
notes: Proved by TestCurrentObservationsControlListsAndPredicates; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A cursor read shares the transaction and stops on cancellation
when: Reads a cursor on the transaction store after an uncommitted create, then reads under a 30 ms context while another session holds an exclusive table lock.
then: Expects the uncommitted row in the transaction's page, and the blocked read to fail within two seconds.
notes: Proved by TestCursorUsesTransactionAndHonorsCancellation; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A binding write outside or after a transaction is refused and a failure blocks commit
when: Calls BindEffect and CloseEffectBinding outside a transaction, ignores a conflicting second registration inside one, uses the retained scope after it closed, sends six invalid inputs, and registers under a canceled context.
then: Expects ErrTransactionRequired, ErrEffectBindingConflict with no row committed, ErrTransactionClosed for the retained scope, ErrEffectBinding for every invalid input, Canceled for the canceled call, and no row in the table.
notes: Proved by TestEffectBindingFailureRollsBackAndRequiresActiveTransaction; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A rejected notification blocks commit
when: For an invalid JSON payload, a duplicate ID, a 33rd message, an oversized payload and a missing queue schema, creates a record and ignores the rejected notification.
then: Expects the transaction to fail, no record committed, and no partial batch.
notes: Proved by TestNotificationFailureRollsBack; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A notification without the outbox peer blocks commit
when: Creates and ignores a notification inside a scope on a store generated without the outbox peer.
then: Expects ErrNotificationsUnavailable and no record committed.
notes: Proved by TestUnavailableNotificationsPreventCommit; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A cleanup observation and its event commit together
when: Observes an owner and notifies in one transaction while the outbox rejects inserts, then repeats after the constraint is removed.
then: Expects the first transaction to fail with no observation kept, and the second to commit the observation with one event.
notes: Proved by TestCleanupObservationAndEventsRollbackTogether; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: Finalization refuses live, incomplete, stale and unsupported resources
when: Tries to finalize a live resource, a deleted but incomplete one and a stale revision, also through direct SQL; completes both owners; finalizes inside a failing transaction, then with its event; reopens an owner; runs SQL that clears or moves the finalization; finalizes an unsupported entity.
then: Expects ErrVersionConflict for the live, incomplete and stale cases, the direct SQL refused, no finalization from the observations alone, nothing kept by the failed transaction, one event with the committed finalization at a higher revision and the same generation, the late observation leaving the finalization time unchanged, both reversal statements refused, and the unsupported entity refused.
notes: Proved by TestDeletionFinalizationIsPermanentAndTransactional; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: Pending deletions appear only under the deleting options and keep access
when: Creates live, pending, finalized, access-denied and access-revoked resources, rebuilds the store, lists with IncludeDeleting and OnlyDeleting under a related access filter page by page, reads CursorVisible and CursorDeleting cursors, and calls Get, Replace and WithLockedResource on the pending and finalized rows.
then: Expects a count of two and pages holding only the live and pending rows, one pending-only count, the cursors returning the same visible IDs, and ErrNotFound without a callback from the three live-only operations.
notes: Proved by TestDeletionFinalizationVisibilityKeepsAccessAndPages; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: Identity and deletion cannot be reversed
when: Changes a row's ID through SQL, soft-deletes it, clears deleted_at and physically deletes it through SQL, and writes to it conditionally at its current revision.
then: Expects the ID change refused, revision 2 after deletion, both reversal statements refused, and ErrVersionConflict for the write.
notes: Proved by TestVersionedIdentityAndDeletionCannotBeReversed; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The ledger records the bootstrap and a restart applies nothing
when: Migrates a fresh schema-generation database, reads the ledger, and migrates again.
then: Expects ledger rows with 001_initial first, and the same row count after the restart.
notes: Proved by TestMigrationLedgerRecordsBootstrapAndRestart; its name or a subtest must carry this ID. Partial: no test yet shows the application role cannot alter the ledger.

title: A new registration is applied once and recorded
when: Migrates, registers a new migration, migrates twice, and applies the same version through ApplyMigration.
then: Expects the new version recorded once and the re-application refused.
notes: Proved by TestMigrationLedgerAppliesNewRegistrations; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: Digest drift and a foreign row are refused
when: Tampers with an applied row's digest and migrates, then restores it, inserts a foreign version, and migrates.
then: Expects ErrMigrationLedger both times.
notes: Proved by TestMigrationLedgerRejectsGapsAndDrift; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: An edited function migration body is refused at startup
when: Migrates, then sets an applied function migration row to the body digest of an earlier source text, and migrates again.
then: Expects ErrMigrationLedger, and expects the refused run to leave the row unchanged.
notes: Proved by TestMigrationLedgerRejectsGapsAndDrift; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A name digest is rewritten once to the body digest
when: Migrates, sets each applied row to the digest of its name, migrates twice, then inserts a foreign row with its name digest and migrates.
then: Expects the first run to rewrite each row to its body digest, the second run to change nothing, and the foreign row to fail with ErrMigrationLedger.
notes: Proved by TestMigrationLedgerRejectsGapsAndDrift; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The emitted pool applies its defaults and bounds
when: Opens a pool with 29 invalid values across the four settings, then reads the defaults, an open limit of 1, and the boundary values 0, 1s and 24h.
then: Expects no pool and the error 'invalid database pool setting: <name>' for every invalid value, the defaults 16, 4, 30m and 5m, an idle default of 1 under an open limit of 1, and every boundary value accepted.
notes: Proved by TestPoolSettingsRejectInvalidValues; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The emitted pool holds its open limit and honors a waiting caller
when: Opens a pool with an open limit of 2 and an idle limit of 1, holds two connections, asks for a third under a 50 ms deadline and then under a canceled context, releases one, pings, and releases the other.
then: Expects no third connection, DeadlineExceeded and Canceled for the two waits, one wait in the statistics, a ping after the release, no connection in use at the end, at most one idle, and a connection closed for the idle limit.
notes: Proved by TestPoolLimitWaitCancellationAndRelease; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The store refuses a missing or altered key index
when: Drops the primary key, drops the key index, recreates it in another column order, recreates it with a predicate, disables the guard, drops NOT NULL and the check constraint, and enables row security, each on a fresh database, then opens the store.
then: Expects the store to refuse to open after each change.
notes: Proved by TestResourceStateSchemaGuard; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The store refuses a disabled revision trigger
when: Disables the revision trigger, opens the store, migrates, and opens it again.
then: Expects the first open refused and the second accepted.
notes: Proved by TestVersionStartupRejectsDisabledTrigger; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A null condition object is refused by the trigger
when: Sets the condition column to JSON null through SQL, then drops the column and opens the store.
then: Expects the null refused and the store refusing to open without the column.
notes: Proved by TestConditionSchemaAndDataAreRequired; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The old code opens the store on the schema at expand and refuses a schema it does not satisfy
when: Migrates a database with a rename and a drop at expand, opens the store with the code of the declaration before the changes, then drops the old column of the rename by hand and opens the store again.
then: Expects the first open to be accepted with the new column, the trigger and the dropped NOT NULL present, and the second to be refused and to name the column.
notes: Level: integration. Not automated yet: schema steps are not built. It runs on PostgreSQL in an unprivileged rootless container, as the other postgresadapter testdata tests do. Planned file internal/generator/postgresadapter/testdata/schema_evolution_test.go. Owner decision of 2026-11-06 (Q3).

title: The code at expand opens the store after the contract of its own changes
when: Migrates a rename and a drop at expand, opens the store with the code at expand, migrates the contract steps, and opens the store with the code at expand again.
then: Expects both opens to be accepted, the second with no old column, no trigger and the new column NOT NULL.

then: Expects an error from the open, and expects the marker pw-MARK-7f3 in no log record, no metric attribute and no error text.
notes: Level: integration. Not automated yet: no test names this ID yet. Planned file internal/generator/postgresadapter/testdata/private_values_test.go. Search the whole recorded output for the marker, also wrapped errors (errors.Unwrap chain) and the driver error text. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): each PostgreSQL server that the test needs runs in a local container without privilege, at the version the test names and a pinned image digest, and the test or its suite starts and removes it.

then: Expects a refusal for an empty configuration, a plaintext issuer, an absent audience, a small modulus and a wrong exponent, and a startup failure for a missing audience, a malformed key and an oversize key file.

title: The emitted verifier refuses oversize and ambiguous tokens
when: Verifies hand-signed tokens with a duplicate payload member, a duplicate header member, an array payload, 34 nesting levels and an oversize length, then sends four invalid header shapes.
then: Expects a refusal for every ambiguous token, and 401 for an absent, unprefixed, wrongly prefixed or repeated header value.

title: The emitted key source refuses an oversize token
when: Starts a key source from an empty, oversize and ambiguous key file, verifies an oversize token, then points the source at a redirecting TLS endpoint and at a plaintext URL.
then: Expects every invalid key file refused, the oversize token refused, the redirect refused with no request to the target, and the plaintext URL refused.

title: The emitted middleware refuses a header without exactly one Bearer credential

then: Expects a refusal for every ambiguous token, and 401 for an absent, unprefixed, wrongly prefixed or repeated header value.

title: A denial from the emitted middleware hides the token and sets no-store and WWW-Authenticate

then: Expects 401 for every fault, 204 for the valid token, no claim from the verifier after a denial, and a denial response with no token, a WWW-Authenticate header and Cache-Control no-store.

title: The emitted verifier reads roles from the configured claim only

then: Expects the verified issuer, subject, profile claims, expiry and selected roles, equal HTTP and shared-context identities, no role from another claim, and a failure for every malformed or oversize role value.

title: The emitted verifier fails authentication on a malformed role claim
when: Verifies a token that holds profile claims, an unselected roles claim and the configured nested role array, then removes and corrupts that array.
then: Expects the verified issuer, subject, profile claims, expiry and selected roles, equal HTTP and shared-context identities, no role from another claim, and a failure for every malformed or oversize role value.

then: Expects the verified issuer, subject, profile claims, expiry and selected roles, equal HTTP and shared-context identities, no role from another claim, and a failure for every malformed or oversize role value.

then: Expects the valid token accepted, every invalid field and document refused, the forged signature refused, no fallback to an unrelated key, and the rotated key accepted.

title: The emitted grant policy permits only a grant that matches every authority dimension
when: Builds a policy from one grant, then asks it for an altered issuer, subject, resource, operation and target, for an admin role caller, for a nil policy and for a zero policy, and reads it from sixteen workers.
then: Expects the exact grant permitted, every altered dimension denied, the role ignored, the nil and zero policies denying, the constructor input copy unchanged, and concurrent reads stable.

title: A nil or zero emitted grant policy denies every operation
when: Builds a policy from one grant, then asks it for an altered issuer, subject, resource, operation and target, for an admin role caller, for a nil policy and for a zero policy, and reads it from sixteen workers.
then: Expects the exact grant permitted, every altered dimension denied, the role ignored, the nil and zero policies denying, the constructor input copy unchanged, and concurrent reads stable.

title: The emitted verifier refuses invalid Unicode in a token payload
when: Signs a payload whose username claim holds an unpaired surrogate escape, in three shapes.
then: Expects every token refused and an empty username in the returned identity.

title: Stop on the emitted key source cancels a retrieval that is already running
when: Holds the key endpoint open inside a refresh that a verification started, then calls Stop twice.
then: Expects the pending verification to return an error inside two seconds, so shutdown cancelled the retrieval.

title: A zero emitted key source denies every token and a repeat Stop is safe
when: Verifies a token against a zero JWKSVerifier value, then calls Stop twice.
then: Expects the token refused and both Stop calls safe.

title: The emitted grant document reader refuses an ambiguous document
when: Parses a valid document, an empty array, and seventeen ambiguous documents that change the member names, the member types, the Unicode, the whitespace, the trailing data and the size.
then: Expects the valid document accepted, the empty array accepted and denying, and every ambiguous document refused with a nil policy.

title: The emitted grant policy refuses a repeated grant and a grant outside its bounds
when: Builds a policy from a repeated grant, from 1,025 grants, and from grants with an empty issuer, an empty subject, an oversize target, a spaced operation and a slashed resource.
then: Expects every construction refused.

title: The emitted grant policy treats an empty target and a literal asterisk target as exact
when: Builds a policy for an empty target and then for a literal asterisk target, and asks each for its own target and for another target.
then: Expects the exact target permitted and the other target denied in both cases.

title: The emitted verifier gives the same identity to concurrent callers
when: Verifies one valid token from sixteen workers, twenty times each.
then: Expects every call to return the same verified subject with no error.

then: Expects Acks of -1 in the produce request, the same payload, the resource key as the record key, and the message ID and kind as headers.
notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC12-OC02-T01, ST-SUP-RC12-OC03-T01.

title: A mutual-TLS publication keeps the message identity
when: Publishes one record with a 0440 private key behind a projected link, and then consumes it from the broker fixture.

title: An unverified broker connection is refused
when: Connects to a broker with a wrong host name, then a wrong trust root, then a wrong client certificate, then no TLS.
then: Expects every connection refused, with valid client options in each case.

title: SCRAM authenticates over TLS and refuses a wrong password

then: Expects the first publication to succeed, the second connection to fail, and no password text in the error.
notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC12-OC06-T01.

title: A failed SCRAM authentication keeps the password private

title: An unbounded SCRAM challenge is refused before key derivation
when: Gives the bounded session six challenges with too many iterations, too few iterations, a repeated field, a missing field and an oversized body.
then: Expects each challenge refused, with no call to the inner session.

title: An uncertain produce closes its client before the next call
when: Blocks the produce request until a 100 ms deadline expires, then releases the broker and publishes again.
then: Expects context.DeadlineExceeded, a prompt return, a different client for the next call, and a successful publication.

title: Only private secret file modes are accepted
when: Gives four unsafe secret file modes and four private modes.
then: Expects each unsafe mode refused and each private mode accepted.

title: Invalid configuration and an invalid trust file fail before the network
when: Gives nine invalid configurations and an invalid trust file.
then: Expects each invalid configuration and the invalid trust file refused before a connection.
notes: Two subtests carry this ID, because the trust file check runs after the secret mode checks.

title: An invalid record payload fails before the network
when: Gives four invalid payloads.
then: Expects each invalid payload refused.

title: A denied publication returns an error
when: Answers the produce request with TopicAuthorizationFailed for every partition.
then: Expects ErrUnavailable from Publish.

title: The runtime refuses a missing queue schema
when: Drops the outbox schema, then builds the runtime with an empty configuration.
then: Expects a construction error that names the schema, before any broker connection.

title: The runtime delivers a message that a former process left
when: Closes the first runtime, commits one message, starts a replacement runtime, and runs it twice.
then: Expects ErrClosed from the closed runtime, one delivery by the replacement, an error from the second run, and the record at the broker.

title: A closed publisher refuses a later publish
when: Publishes from 16 goroutines, closes the publisher twice, and publishes again.
then: Expects every goroutine to return, no fault from the repeated close, and ErrClosed from the last publish.

title: A committed message reaches TLS Kafka and leaves the queue
when: Enqueues one message with an application row in one transaction, waits, commits, and then consumes the record.
then: Expects no broker call before the commit, one delivery after it, an empty queue, the retained application row, the expanded JSONB payload, and the durable message ID in a header.

title: The producer registers as one destination handler of the outbox

notes: Level: unit. Not automated yet: no test names this ID yet. Planned file internal/generator/kafkaproducer/generator_test.go.

title: The producer publishes claimed outbox rows only
given: The declaration of ST-SUP-RC12-OC17-T01, a real PostgreSQL 16 server and a fake Kafka broker that records each record.
when: Enqueues one message in a transaction that rolls back, one that commits, and one that commits while another worker holds its claim, and runs the producer.
then: Expects only the claimed committed message published, the rolled-back one never, and the one claimed by the other worker not published by this producer.
notes: Level: integration. Not automated yet: no test names this ID yet. Planned file internal/generator/kafkaproducer/testdata/integration_test.go. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): each PostgreSQL server that the test needs runs in a local container without privilege, at the version the test names and a pinned image digest, and the test or its suite starts and removes it.

title: The kafka-producer component is refused when no component provides the durable-outbox port
given: A service declaration with the kafka-producer component and no durable-events mixin.
when: Checks, with the compiler in process as stego check does, a declaration that binds kafka-producer in a registry copy where no component of the active set provides durable-outbox; then the same declaration with the outbox component in the active set.
then: Expects the first check to exit non-zero with a refusal that names kafka-producer and the port durable-outbox, and the second to pass.
notes: Level: unit. Not automated yet: no test names this ID yet. Planned file internal/generator/kafkaproducer/generator_test.go. The statement follows the component's requires (registry/components/kafka-producer/component.yaml lists durable-outbox), as decided for the apply of the Supplying contract plan.

then: Expects the credential returned for the valid case only, no credential read or grant request for a public, disabled or subject-less client, and ErrOwnership with no grant when the owner changes.

then: Expects the safe callbacks accepted, every unsafe callback refused, every invalid policy refused, and no provider request for an invalid policy.

then: Expects the nine unsafe flags false, no secret in the request, confirmation through a read of the saved ID, no request to the foreign location, ErrConflict for the repeat, and no replayed creation.

then: Expects the nine unsafe flags false, no secret in the request, confirmation through a read of the saved ID, no request to the foreign location, ErrConflict for the repeat, and no replayed creation.

title: The emitted binding helpers refuse a foreign or partly owned client with ErrOwnership
when: Binds a live client that holds the current ownership keys, then one that holds the complete legacy form, then five records with a nil client, a foreign name, mixed ownership, partial ownership and a wrong id.
then: Expects the current and complete legacy forms accepted, and ErrOwnership for every other record, including a client with no ownership key and a client with a foreign reserved key.

title: The emitted client search refuses an invalid fragment or page before any request

then: Expects one request with the encoded fragment, the fixed search mode and the selected page, every invalid fragment and page refused, and no network request for an invalid argument.

then: Expects the composed client name, the ownership keys under the reserved prefix, the legacy form and its rename map, no legacy form for a kind that declares none, and ErrOwnership for an empty id.

title: The emitted audience binding accepts a stored name for the legacy form only
when: Binds a legacy audience record by its stored public name, then binds a migrated record by that same stored name, then binds the migrated record by its generated name.
then: Expects the legacy form accepted, ErrOwnership for the migrated record under the stored name, and the generated name accepted.

title: A failed search from the emitted provider is not repeated or widened
when: Searches against a provider that denies the query, returns null, returns too many records and returns a repeated record.
then: Expects an error in each case, ErrResponse for the three invalid bodies, exactly one read, and no fall back to another query.

title: The emitted provider refuses an ambiguous provider response with ErrResponse
when: Reads one client and then looks one up against eleven invalid response bodies.
then: Expects ErrResponse for a null body, an empty object, a different ID, a duplicate member, invalid Unicode, trailing data, a duplicate attribute, a repeated record, a foreign record and an empty ID.

title: An invalid administrator grant never reaches the emitted provider API
when: Answers the token endpoint with five grants that have no token type, a wrong type, a zero lifetime, an oversize lifetime and a duplicate member.
then: Expects ErrResponse in each case and no API request.

title: The emitted provider checks identifiers and pages before any request and stays in its realm
when: Looks up, pages and inspects clients, then reads seven unsafe identifiers and four invalid pages.
then: Expects every request inside the selected realm with the administrator credential, every unsafe identifier and invalid page refused, no network request for an invalid argument, and a cached administrator token.

title: The emitted provider does not treat a record with no explicit state as disabled
when: Disables a client whose record omits the enabled member and then whose record holds a null enabled member.
then: Expects ErrResponse in both cases and no write.

title: Credential rotation and an unauthorized answer clear the emitted provider token cache
when: Reads a client, replaces the private credential file, reads again while the provider answers 401 with a private body, then reads once more.
then: Expects the rotated secret used for the next grant, the unauthorized read failed without the provider body and without a replay, and a new grant for the later read.

title: Close and cancellation release every caller of the emitted provider
when: Holds the first authentication open, then calls with a canceled context, then with a short deadline, then closes the provider.
then: Expects the canceled caller released with context.Canceled, the waiting caller released with context.DeadlineExceeded, the first call canceled by Close, and ErrClosed for later work.

title: A span from the emitted provider keeps the caller trace and holds no request data
when: Reads a client through the provider inside a sampled caller span and inspects the provider request headers and the two recorded spans.
then: Expects the caller trace kept with a new span ID, no baggage or trace state sent, client spans with the response status, and no client name, provider ID, server URL or credential in the attributes.

title: The emitted lifecycle saves a prepared closure without a provider call
when: Prepares closure for a known provider ID with current and with legacy ownership, repeats it after a restart, then prepares with another ID and reconciles.
then: Expects the closure saved with that ID and no provider call, the journal unchanged on repeat, ErrClientLifecycle for the other ID, ErrClientClosed on reconcile, and the later close to delete the client.
notes: Proved by TestServiceAccountLifecyclePrepareClosure; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The emitted lifecycle closes a current-ownership client found by its saved ID
when: Closes a client that the provider holds under current ownership while the application also declares legacy keys, directly and after a prepared closure.
then: Expects the provider calls delete, inspect, delete only, the journal bound to the saved ID with closure kept, a repeat that changes nothing, a late client deleted, and reconcile refused with ErrClientClosed.
notes: Proved by TestServiceAccountLifecycleObservedClosure; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: The emitted lifecycle refuses closure of a foreign or unconfirmed client

then: Expects the closure refused, the provider client kept, the closure intent and ID kept, no unconfirmed binding saved, and no discovery or access call.
notes: Proved by TestServiceAccountLifecycleObservedClosureRejectsForeignOwnership; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A rejected or lost save stops the emitted closure until a retry

then: Expects the closure refused with the client kept and the intent saved, and a retry after the save works that deletes the client.
notes: Proved by TestServiceAccountLifecycleObservedClosureSaveFailure; its name or a subtest must carry this ID.

title: A malformed write query fails before a request

title: A rejected write is not retried
when: The generated client sends a POST, a PUT and a PATCH with a caller query that already selects weaker validation, then sends two writes with a malformed query.
then: The server receives exactly three writes, so no rejected write is retried.

title: A computed patch is not retried after a conflict

then: The server sees exactly one PATCH, and the conflict comes back unretried.

title: A watch reconnect reads the replaced token file
when: A fake API server returns a two-page list, one watch event, a bookmark, an expired-history error, and a later list and delete, while the token file changes during observation.
then: The reconnect uses the replaced token.

title: A replaced token file takes effect on the next request
when: The client makes a request, the test writes a new token to the same file, and the client makes another request.
then: The server sees the new bearer token without a client restart.

title: Discovery reads the token file again for each call
when: The requirement check passes once, then the token file is replaced and the server stops reporting the resource, and the check runs again.
then: The second call uses the new bearer token.

title: The emitted client reads a rotated projected token on a live cluster

given: A service declaration with the kubernetes-service component and the modes api, worker and controller (one controller replica), generated into a temporary folder, with the generated renderer run.

The statement names no readiness probe and no upper bound for controller; the probe and the lease TTL bound of the first draft were removed. Slow the checkpoint write with a lock held by the test, so that a grace period too short for the release is caught. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): each PostgreSQL server that the test needs runs in a local container without privilege, at the version the test names and a pinned image digest, and the test or its suite starts and removes it.

title: The emitted runtime does not export to an untrusted collector

title: The emitted runtime finishes shutdown inside its limit when the collector is blocked
when: Observes three times the queue size in requests against a collector that never answers, then closes the runtime.
then: Expects every request to keep its status, the whole request set to finish inside one second, an export failure to be recorded, and shutdown to finish inside its limit.

title: The emitted runtime attaches the collector token to every signal

title: The emitted runtime applies a replaced collector token without a restart
when: Exports traces, logs and metrics to a TLS collector that requires one bearer token, replaces the token file, exports again, then makes the token file world readable.

title: The emitted runtime refuses a collector token file that others can read
when: Exports traces, logs and metrics to a TLS collector that requires one bearer token, replaces the token file, exports again, then makes the token file world readable.
then: Expects every signal accepted with the first token, every signal accepted with the replacement token without a restart, and a refused export after the file permission change.

title: The emitted runtime identity is a UUID v4 from the random source
when: Builds an instance ID from a fixed 17-byte reader, then from a short reader and from a reader that returns an error.
then: Expects the canonical UUID v4 encoding from exactly 16 bytes, and an empty value with fixed error text that holds no private detail for each failing reader.

title: The emitted runtime fails with fixed text on an entropy failure

then: Expects the canonical UUID v4 encoding from exactly 16 bytes, and an empty value with fixed error text that holds no private detail for each failing reader.

then: Expects the active counter at one for the open stream, no more than the series limit of histogram series, an overflow series that keeps every count, and the active counter back at zero.

title: The emitted active request counter returns to zero

then: Expects the active counter at one for the open stream, no more than the series limit of histogram series, an overflow series that keeps every count, and the active counter back at zero.

title: Concurrent and replacement emitted runtimes hold distinct identities

then: Expects thirty-two valid and distinct UUID identities, and no change to an identity across its close.

then: Expects the panic re-raised, no status attribute on the duration metric, error.type panic, the active counter at zero, an ERROR log record, and no private value in the export.

then: Expects the panic re-raised, no status attribute on the duration metric, error.type panic, the active counter at zero, an ERROR log record, and no private value in the export.

then: Expects one completion for each call, the private outcome recorded as the fixed failure value, correlated client spans, idempotent completion, and no private value in the export.

when: Builds the runtime for nine invalid exporter and interval values, then records three times the queue size of calls against a collector that never answers, then closes the runtime, then disables both signals.
then: Expects every invalid setting refused, the calls not delayed, the export failures counted, shutdown inside one shared limit, and no provider for a disabled signal.

then: Expects every invalid setting refused, the calls not delayed, the export failures counted, shutdown inside one shared limit, and no provider for a disabled signal.

title: The emitted queue commits the message with the application write
when: Writes an application row and enqueues one message in one transaction, then rolls back, and then repeats the same work and commits.
then: Expects no visible data before the end of the transaction, no row and no message after the rollback, and both after the commit.

title: The emitted queue refuses an invalid payload before it uses the database
when: Validates ten invalid payloads, one valid payload, an enqueue with no transaction and a queue with no database.
then: Expects every invalid payload refused, the valid payload accepted, and an error for the missing transaction and the missing database.

title: A retry holds only its own key
when: Claims two messages for one resource key and one for another key, retries the oldest message, and claims again.
then: Expects no claim for the successor during the delay, the same ID and a second attempt after it, and progress for the other key.
notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC18-OC04-T01.

title: A retry keeps the message identity
when: Claims two messages for one resource key and one for another key, retries the oldest message, and claims again.

notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC18-OC03-T01.

title: A worker retry keeps the message identity
when: Fails the first delivery of one message with an error that holds a private value, then lets both messages succeed.
then: Expects three handler calls in order, the same ID for both attempts, one retry, no lost lease, and an empty queue.
notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC18-OC06-T02.

title: An expired lease cannot acknowledge or retry a message
when: Claims one message with a short lease, waits for the lease to expire, then acknowledges and retries with the old receipt.
then: Expects both calls to report no effect and the message to stay in the queue.

title: A changed lease token cannot acknowledge a message
when: Replaces the lease token in the database while the handler runs.
then: Expects one lost lease, no delivery, and the retained message.

title: The emitted worker stores no handler error text
when: Runs the worker with a handler that returns an error which holds a private value.
then: Expects the stored failure code 'delivery-failed' and no part of the handler's error text.

title: A worker retry stores no error text
when: Fails the first delivery of one message with an error that holds a private value, then lets both messages succeed.
then: Expects three handler calls in order, the same ID for both attempts, one retry, no lost lease, and an empty queue.
notes: The function's assertions prove several contracts together. Each subtest runs the whole body. The other subtests are ST-SUP-RC18-OC04-T02.

title: A result after the attempt deadline is not acknowledged
when: Runs the worker with a handler that waits for its context to end and then returns success.
then: Expects no delivery count, a retry, and the stored failure code 'delivery-timeout'.

title: An attempt deadline retains the failed message
when: Runs a handler that waits for its context to end.
then: Expects the attempt to stop at its deadline and the message to stay in the queue for retry.

title: A claim with a lost client result returns no delivery
when: Runs the claim through a bounded SQL driver that returns a query error, and then a row error after one row.
then: Expects no delivery in both cases and the underlying error for the caller.

title: Recovery after an unknown claim result keeps the delivery contract
when: Loses the claim result, waits for normal lease expiry, and claims the message again.
then: Expects the same message IDs and contents, a higher attempt count, a new receipt token, and no effect from the old token.

title: A lost notice session stops the source and its subscriptions
when: Terminates the dedicated PostgreSQL backend of the source, then reads the subscription, subscribes again, and starts a replacement source.
then: Expects the supervised task and the subscription to fail with ErrEventSourceUnavailable, the failed source to refuse a new subscription, and the replacement source to deliver the next notice.

title: A repeated message ID stops the application write
when: Enqueues one message, then writes an application row and enqueues the same message ID in one transaction.
then: Expects the enqueue to fail, the commit to fail, no application row, and one stored message.

title: Notices reach every session after the commit, in commit order
when: Subscribes two separate sessions, enqueues inside an open transaction, commits, and then enqueues two messages for one resource key in one transaction.
then: Expects no notice before the commit, the notice in both sessions after it, and the two notices in commit order.

title: Concurrent enqueues serialize before the sequence
when: Enqueues for one resource key in one open transaction, then enqueues the same key in a second transaction, and commits the first.
then: Expects the second enqueue to wait for the predecessor, and expects the first message in the next claim.

title: Concurrent workers claim distinct messages
when: Runs eight workers that each claim eight of 32 queued messages.
then: Expects no error, 32 claimed messages, and no message in two batches.

title: An unknown destination stays in the queue
when: Enqueues a message for a destination that the worker has no handler for.
then: Expects the stored code 'destination-unknown', no handler call, and the unknown-destination counter above zero.

title: Unsafe worker limits are refused and the retry delay stays bounded
when: Builds the worker with seven unsafe configurations and with a nil handler, then samples the retry delay for four attempt counts.
then: Expects an error for each unsafe input, and every delay inside the configured bounds.

title: The worker holds its concurrency limit and copies its handlers
when: Queues eight messages, removes the handler from the caller's map after construction, and starts a second run.
then: Expects at most two active handlers, all eight deliveries, no active handler at the end, and an error from the second run.

title: A database failure drops no message
when: Closes the connection pool while the worker runs.
then: Expects the database-failure counter above zero and no delivery.

title: The blocked view holds one entry for each stuck key
when: Claims two of four messages, reads the blocked view, retries one key with a failure code, makes that key ready, and reads the view again with two invalid limits.
then: Expects one entry for each in-flight key with its destination and timing, the failure code retained, the ready key absent, and both invalid limits refused.

title: Dead letters and purge keep the unexhausted messages
when: Exhausts one resource key with three claims and retries, parks one message by a permanent refusal and one from an unknown outcome, lists the dead letters, purges them, and gives an invalid limit.
then: Expects the three parked messages listed, the one from an unknown outcome kept by the purge until a person resolves it, the others removed, the fresh message retained, and the invalid limit refused.

title: A process crash commits nothing and releases its lease
when: Runs a helper subprocess that exits abruptly with an open transaction, and again with an active claim.
then: Expects no application row and no message after the first exit, and recovery of the same message with a higher attempt count after the lease expires.

title: The event source holds its subscription and queue bounds
when: Overruns the buffer of a slow subscription, fills the subscription limit, cancels one subscription, and closes the source.
then: Expects ErrSlowConsumer for the slow reader, ErrEventCapacity at the limit, the cancellation returned, and ErrEventSourceUnavailable after the close.

title: Shutdown acknowledges a delivery that completed
when: Cancels the worker while its handler runs, and lets the handler return success after the cancellation.
then: Expects the worker to wait for the handler, one delivery, and an empty queue.

title: A canceled claim returns the cancellation
when: Claims with a context that is already canceled.
then: Expects context.Canceled from the claim.
